domain: Transportation Systems / Institutional Coordination / Technology Lock-In
topic_summary: Analysis of the convention determining which side of the road vehicles travel on, focusing on right-hand driving as the globally dominant standard. Examines the coordination mechanisms, path dependencies, and switching costs that stabilize this convention despite its arbitrary origins.

key_entities.name: Right-Hand Traffic Convention
key_entities.role: Dominant global standard for road traffic direction

key_entities.name: Left-Hand Traffic Convention
key_entities.role: Minority global standard retained in former British territories and Japan

key_entities.name: National Transportation Authorities
key_entities.role: Enforcers of traffic conventions within territorial boundaries

key_entities.name: Cross-Border Travelers
key_entities.role: Actors who must navigate handedness transitions

key_claims.content: The choice between right and left-hand traffic has no inherent physical or safety advantage
Value of a handedness convention increases with number of adopters
Changing handedness requires coordinated replacement of infrastructure, vehicles, and driver habits
Right-hand traffic has become the dominant global standard through colonial diffusion and economic pressure

key_tensions.nature: Pressure for global uniformity conflicts with national autonomy to set traffic rules
Theoretical efficiency gains from universal standard blocked by switching costs

key_mechanisms.description: Each additional adopter of a handedness standard increases value for all existing adopters through reduced cognitive load at borders and standardized vehicle production
State monopoly on legitimate violence enforces handedness convention through traffic law
Physical road design (signs, lane markings, intersection geometry) embeds handedness assumption

key_absences.description: No analysis of whether pedestrian flow conventions (sidewalk passing norms) align with vehicular handedness
No examination of whether right-hand dominance in human population interacts with steering wheel placement

axes.structural_delta: The value of adopting a handedness convention scales with the number of prior adopters, creating self-reinforcing equilibria
axes.primary_observable: Adoption rate over time; switching cost magnitude relative to coordination benefit
axes.selection_reason: Upstream coordination mechanism; structurally distinct from physical infrastructure and manufacturing constraints

axes.structural_delta: Road geometry, signage, and intersection design physically encode handedness assumptions, creating material switching costs
axes.primary_observable: Capital stock replacement cost; infrastructure redesign requirements for handedness switch
axes.selection_reason: Different observable (physical capital vs coordination benefit); independent epsilon source

axes.structural_delta: Vehicle production optimizes for dominant handedness standard, creating economies of scale that penalize minority conventions
axes.primary_observable: Price differential between RHT and LHT vehicles; production volume ratios
axes.selection_reason: Downstream synthesis of coordination effect; distinct extractive mechanism via production economics

axes.structural_delta: Coordinated replacement of infrastructure, vehicle fleet, and driver habits creates prohibitive one-time cost
axes.primary_observable: Historical switching attempts (Sweden 1967, Samoa 2009); cost-benefit analyses of proposed switches
axes.selection_reason: Highest centrality; downstream synthesis node capturing cumulative lock-in effect

axes.structural_delta: Cognitive load and accident risk at borders between different handedness regimes
axes.primary_observable: Accident rates at handedness-transition borders; driver error frequency in rental vehicles
axes.selection_reason: Independent observable (safety hazard vs coordination benefit); distinct epsilon from other axes

omegas.description: Does pedestrian flow convention (sidewalk passing norms) align with vehicular handedness? If misaligned, is there a safety cost? Absence noted in extraction but not structurally central to vehicular coordination.

Does right-hand dominance in ~90% of human population interact with steering wheel placement to create safety or efficiency differentials? If so, the 'arbitrary origin' claim weakens and coordination_equilibrium may have a weak physical substrate.

Was right-hand traffic dominance achieved through colonial imposition (extractive) or voluntary adoption (coordination)? Historical mechanism unclear; affects classification of coordination_equilibrium as rope vs tangled_rope.

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Five axes survived independence testing with distinct observables and epsilon sources. Coordination_equilibrium and infrastructure_embedding are upstream; manufacturing_standardization and switching_cost_barrier are downstream synthesis nodes; border_friction is independent safety dimension.
